items.statement:
Let $R\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be upper triangular with nonzero diagonal, $y\in\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, and $(n+3)u<1$. Compute descending substitution by the sequential rounded dot $s_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{j>i}R_{ij}\widehat x_j)$ (empty sum zero), $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(y_i-s_i)$, and $\widehat x_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/R_{ii})$. If every operation succeeds, there is upper triangular $\Delta R$ with
$$(R+\Delta R)\widehat x=y,\qquad |\Delta R|\le\gamma_{n+3}|R|,\qquad \|\Delta R\|_F\le\gamma_{n+3}\|R\|_F.$$
In particular $\widehat x=0$ forces $y=0$. Forward substitution has the transposed conclusion.
items.strategy:
1.1 Expand the rounded dot to obtain $s_i=\sum_{j>i}R_{ij}\widehat x_j(1+\theta_{ij})$, with $|\theta_{ij}|\le\gamma_{n-i}$, and use $s_n=0$. Write subtraction and division errors as $\alpha_i,\beta_i\in[-u,u]$. The computed row identity is then $R_{ii}\widehat x_i/((1+\alpha_i)(1+\beta_i))+\sum_{j>i}R_{ij}\widehat x_j(1+\theta_{ij})=y_i$. These identities also hold for zero intermediates by taking the corresponding error zero. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 Choose $\Delta R_{ii}=R_{ii}(((1+\alpha_i)(1+\beta_i))^{-1}-1)$ and $\Delta R_{ij}=R_{ij}\theta_{ij}$ for $j>i$, with zeros below the diagonal. Since $u<1/(n+3)\le1/4$, all denominators are positive and $|((1+\alpha_i)(1+\beta_i))^{-1}-1|\le(1-u)^{-2}-1\le3u/(1-3u)=\gamma_3$; multiplying positive denominators verifies the last inequality. Thus every entry has the claimed bound. [F1, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

2.1 Step 1.1 gives $(R+\Delta R)\widehat x=y$, and summing the squared entry bounds gives the Frobenius estimate. If $\widehat x=0$, the same equation gives $y=0$, including dimension one without a division by $\|\widehat x\|$. Reversing the row order proves the lower-triangular version. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Rounded matrix products give certified linear and normal-equation residual allowances
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, $x\in\mathbb F^n$, $y\in\mathbb F^m$ have stored real or complex entries, with $m,n\ge1$. Use the operationwise arithmetic model, successful sequential dot products, and $0<u<1$ with $(\max(m,n)-1)u<1$. Define
$$g_k=\frac{1+6u}{1-(k-1)u}-1,\qquad F=\|A\|_F,\quad X=\|x\|_2,\quad Y=\|y\|_2.$$
For $\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(Ax)$ and $\widehat w=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-y)$, put $V=g_nFX$ and $W=V+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+Y)$. Then
$$\|\widehat w-(Ax-y)\|_2\le W.$$
For a stored real $\lambda>0$, also compute $\widehat z=\operatorname{fl}(A^*\widehat w)$, $\widehat l=\operatorname{fl}(\lambda x)$ and $\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat z+\widehat l)$, rounding scalar multiplication componentwise. The exact intended normal residual $r=A^*(Ax-y)+\lambda x$ satisfies
$$\|\widehat r-r\|_2\le\rho:=FW+g_mF\|\widehat w\|_2+u\lambda X+u(\|\widehat z\|_2+\|\widehat l\|_2).$$
Norms in these certificates mean exact norms or certified upper bounds. Uncontrolled rounding of the certificate itself is not authorized. The linear bound applies columnwise to certify $\|I-AB\|_2\le\|I-AB\|_F$ from stored basis-solve columns $B$.
items.strategy:
1.1 For $(a+ib)(c+id)$, each rounded real product has error at most $u$ times its absolute exact value. Each final real addition contributes at most $u(1+u)$ times the two corresponding product magnitudes. The Euclidean norm of the resulting real/imaginary error is at most $2(2u+u^2)|a+ib||c+id|\le6u|a+ib||c+id|$, since $u<1$. Conjugation is exact. Real products obey this conservative bound as well. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 In a length-$k$ dot product, each product error from step 1.1 is propagated through at most $k-1$ additions. Expansion of each real component and [F2] bound the dot discrepancy by $[6u+\gamma_{k-1}(1+6u)]\sum_i|a_i||x_i|=g_k\sum_i|a_i||x_i|$, with $\gamma_0=0$. Combining rows and applying Cauchy-Schwarz gives $\|\widehat v-Ax\|_2\le g_nFX=V$. Componentwise subtraction has vector error at most $u(\|\widehat v\|_2+Y)$, so the linear residual allowance is $W$. Zeros cause no difficulty in this expansion. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Apply step 1.2 to $A^*\widehat w$ to get $\|\widehat z-A^*\widehat w\|_2\le g_mF\|\widehat w\|_2$. Transporting the earlier error through $A^*$ adds at most $FW$. The scalar product error is at most $u\lambda X$; the last addition adds at most $u(\|\widehat z\|_2+\|\widehat l\|_2)$. Their sum proves $\rho$. For basis columns, the triangle inequality combines each computed linear residual with its allowance; summing the squared column bounds gives a Frobenius certificate for $I-AB$, which bounds its induced Euclidean norm by Cauchy-Schwarz. [F1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎
